result:
I found and fixed 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings. A script that compares every rule (1–150) against what its docstring describes now finds no differences. It tested about 1,500 (quantity, unit price) pairs per rule; it doesn't prove correctness for every possible input.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 13, 91, 138 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, but the module docstring says to round down | Changed to `// 100` |
| 14, 33 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000 won, so discounts between 100,000 and 200,000 weren't capped | Always cap at 100,000 |
| 21 | Cap was applied to the price before the discount was worked out; the docstring caps the discount | Work out the discount, then cap it at 10,000 |
| 35 | Used 4% instead of 3% | Changed to 3% |
| 115 | Used 16% instead of 15% | Changed to 15% |
| 137 | Used 9% instead of 8% | Changed to 8% |
| 111 | Discount started above 20 units (`qty > 20`) instead of at 20 | Changed to `qty >= 20` |

Rules 72 (`qty > 10`) and 123 (`qty >= 101`) are written differently from the docstring but give the same results. Both are "marginal" rules, where the discount covers only units above the threshold, so at exactly the threshold the discount is 0 either way. I left them unchanged.

STATUS: DONE
